name: Percival

attributes.attribute: son of Herzeloyde and Gahmuret the plain knight
he cup of the Last Supper sought in the quest

sources: Loomis, Roger Sherman. *The Grail from Celtic Myth to Christian Symbol.* New York: Columbia University Press, 1963.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Percival is a hero of the Arthurian tales. He was son of the Welsh princess Herzeloyde and the warrior Gahmuret, and grew up in a cottage knowing nothing of his shining family. He became a knight noted for his plainness and purity. The quest for the Grail, the cup of the Last Supper, is the great tale that holds him. He wandered in a barren land ruled by the wounded Fisher King, who could only fish. He had a vision of a cup and a bleeding lance, but said nothing. The vision left him alone in the wood. He returned to King Arthur's court, and the knights set off on their own quests. In time he found the Grail castle again and asked the right questions: whose cup, why the bleeding lance. The king was healed, the land bloomed, and Percival sat on the reborn throne. Chretien de Troyes wrote of him in 1175.

okr.objective: Summarize Percival as the grail hero of the Arthurian tales.
